_comment: Scene geometry, single source of truth shared by the Blender build script and
the project's own tooling. Blender runs its own bundled Python and cannot import
packages.schemas, so the numbers live here in JSON rather than being duplicated
in two places and drifting.
Transcribed from docs/dataset/scene-spec.md. If a value here disagrees with the
spec, the spec is authoritative and this file is wrong.
Units are metres. Right-handed, Z up, origin at the south-west floor corner.

racking._comment: 2.6 m deliberately: tall enough to occlude a person from a wall-mounted camera, short enough that the ceiling-mounted CAM_C still sees over them.

cameras._comment: Moved from (4,14,4.5) after render verification: the original sight line to (12,8,0) passed RACK_2 at z=1.88 m against a 2.6 m rack and was fully blocked. Now mounted on the north edge of the aisle at the west end, looking east toward the intersection.

camera_optics._comment: 25.7 mm on a 36 mm sensor is about 70 degrees horizontal. Rectilinear: no barrel distortion, whatever the visual references show.

_comment: Primitives are authored at the real object's footprint, not at a convenient box
size. A CC0 asset dropped in later scales into the same bounding volume, so zone
polygons and camera coverage never need re-checking because of the swap.
Colours are not decorative. They were chosen by searching OKLCH space under two
constraints: every entity at least 0.15 OKLab from every surface, and at least
0.17 from every other entity. The original hand-picked set had nine collisions,
including a hi-vis worker 0.025 from the floor paint and a forklift 0.013 from
it, which made both nearly invisible against the floor they stood on.
Hues are restricted to plausible warehouse colours: an unconstrained search
returned a magenta forklift, which separates well and looks absurd.
max_speed_mps is the top speed from scene spec 5; E5.3 uses it to bound how far a hand-over between cameras can travel in the blind interval.
Per-actor colour overrides, keyed by entity id (ids are stable across cases).
Any actor not listed renders in its class colour. Scene spec 5 requires a
distinct vest colour per actor so appearance features (E5.2) have signal;
the first render shipped one colour per class and P01/P02 were pixel-identical.
Chosen by the same constrained OKLCH search as the class palette: at least 0.15
from every surface, 0.17 from every other class, 0.12 from the actor's own class,
within a plausible hue band (hi-vis orange vest; navy forklift, yellow collides
with the floor paint).

render._comment: EEVEE rather than Cycles: path tracing buys realism the detector does not need and costs hours per case. Object index and depth passes are consumed in-process and never written to disk.
render._engine_note: Blender 4.2 called this BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT; 5.x reverted to BLENDER_EEVEE. build_scene.py falls back rather than failing on the rename.

lighting._comment: Constant across all six cases so a detection failure is attributable to the scene rather than to the light. No skylights, no daylight, whatever the visual reference shows.

_comment: Surface colours, shared with the separation check. The wall is deliberately
darker than a real warehouse: a near-white AMR against a pale wall cannot be
separated at all (best achievable 0.109 against a 0.15 floor), and darkening
the wall was the only fix that kept the robot a plausible colour.
